tender.title: Technology and Data Professional Services Framework
tender.description:
Ordnance Survey (OS) requires Suppliers to provide technology and data professional services to support the delivery of its strategic objectives, transformation programmes, products, services and operational requirements.
The Suppliers shall deliver specialist technology and data expertise through a multi-lot framework agreement, providing access to suitably qualified professionals across a range of disciplines, including software engineering, geospatial applications, testing services and artificial intelligence. The framework will provide OS with a flexible and efficient route to market for the procurement of specialist resources and services required to support projects, programmes, service delivery and business change activities.
The scope of the Framework includes, but is not limited to:
• Provision of specialist resources and teams to support the design, development, implementation, enhancement and maintenance of geospatial applications and data solutions.
• Provision of software development services to support digital products, online services, APIs, data integration, data processing, data sharing and related technology capabilities.
• Provision of functional and non-functional testing services, including quality assurance, test automation, performance testing, security testing and associated testing activities.
• Provision of artificial intelligence and machine learning services, including the design, development and deployment of AI-enabled solutions, agentic systems and other advanced AI capabilities.
The Framework is intended to support OS in achieving improved delivery capability, enhanced service resilience, increased organisational agility, innovation, operational efficiency and the successful delivery of strategic technology and data initiatives.
The successful Suppliers will be expected to work collaboratively with OS and relevant stakeholders to ensure the continuous delivery, improvement and optimisation of services throughout the Framework term. Suppliers will be required to provide resources that align with OS-defined role profiles, capability standards and specific business requirements.
The Authority may require flexibility to accommodate changes in demand, technological developments, legislative requirements, organisational priorities, emerging technologies and future business needs during the Framework term.
The Framework is to be divided into four Lots:
• Lot 1: Geospatial Applications
• Lot 2: General Software Development
• Lot 3: General Testing Services
• Lot 4: AI Services
Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots. It is anticipated that up to three Suppliers will be appointed to each Lot. Call-off contracts may be awarded through either further competition or direct award in accordance with the Framework Agreement. OS does not guarantee any minimum level of spend under the Framework.
Further details of the requirements are contained within the procurement documents.

The approach encompasses the deployment of a selection of temporary and permanent camera units, the installation of two new CCTV columns, and the installation of two external communications cabinets. Permanent equipment will be positioned in areas where site layout is confirmed, while temporary placements are designated for high risk zones (e.g., hoardings) pending finalisation of AfA/ticket office plans and be relocated as required.  Furthermore, it is anticipated that the Marlowe cameras will remain operational until the definitive station configuration is established and the overall CCTV design is refined. This ensures that the coverage and functionality currently provided by the Marlowe cameras will be maintained through the strategic placement of new camera units, as temporary positions at the hoardings do not offer adequate surveillance to fully replace the Marlowe system. This option uses completed ES5 designs, IDC/IDR signoff, AFC drawings and a full bill of materials.

tender.description:
The Department for Education (DfE) has awarded a contract to a Supplier to support the establishment and early operation of five new Regional Care Cooperatives (RCCs) and to deliver the expanded Fostering Recruitment and Retention Programme.
Regional Care Cooperatives
Every child deserves safe, high-quality care close to home. Regional care cooperatives (RCCs) will help make this a reality by transforming the approach local areas take to commissioning and providing homes for children in care. Further background on RCCs and the policy intent behind this reform can be found here: Regional care cooperatives policy statement - GOV.UK
The Delivery Partner will provide structured coaching, facilitation, and technical expertise to support regions through the RCC staged progression model-Foundation and Development-so that they are prepared to transition into Delivery, as set out in the RCC Design Specification Guidance here Apply to set up a regional care cooperative - GOV.UK This will include support for:
• diagnostics, planning and governance
• co design and development of sufficiency strategies
• market shaping approaches
• adoption of the national common data model
• establishment of core regional functions for sustainable forecasting and commissioning
Further information please see tender documentation.
Fostering Recruitment and Retention Programme
The Delivery Partner will also support the next phase of the Fostering Recruitment and Retention Programme, delivered under the same contract as the RCC support package. In this expanded phase, Fostering Hubs will progress beyond initial applicant engagement to manage the entire recruitment and approval process, creating a more integrated and end to end model of recruiting, assessing, and supporting foster carers. The programme contributes to the Department's ambition to secure homes for 10,000 more children by 2029. Fostering Hubs guidance and application forms can be found here Fostering Programme: New Hubs Expression of Interest - GOV-UK Find a grant.
The Delivery Partner will provide subject matter expertise in fostering recruitment and retention, alongside support to hubs in establishing performance monitoring and reporting mechanisms, delivering change management, and offering troubleshooting support as programme and/or LA level issues emerge. Support may include stakeholder relationship facilitation, HR related assistance, and co production of assessing social worker practice models. For new hubs, the Delivery Partner will provide challenge, independent oversight, and practical support through design and implementation. All support should be designed to build long term capability within hubs.
The Delivery Partner will work with approximately 100 participating LAs across new and existing hubs. The successful organisation will be expected to ensure strategic alignment between RCCs and Fostering Hubs, working closely with RCC leadership where established, and supporting areas to integrate hubs into RCCs as the system evolves. The long term vision is for every local authority to be part of an RCC.

LNER has been publicly owned and operated by the Department for Transport's Operator of Last Resort since 24th June 2018 and is a wholly owned subsidiary of DfT Operator Limited (DfTO). 
LNER operates within a public sector governance framework and works closely with its suppliers to deliver safe, reliable and value for money rail services.
DFTO is committed to working closely with all aspects of the rail industry to ensure the continued provision of critical passenger rail services.
FPA Consulting Limited (hereinafter referenced as FPA) has been employed by LNER to act as procurement consultant and advisor to LNER for this procurement. In the event of a contract award, the successful Bidder will enter into a direct contract with LNER and not FPA.
LNER proposes to enter into one contract with the successful Bidder for a 12-month period from 1st April 2027 with contract extension options for a further period of 12-months followed by 12-months giving a maximum potential period of 36-months.

- Participation (Invitation to Participate)
- Commercial Invitation to Negotiate (Invitation to Tender)
Each of the above stages are split into specific stages, outlined below. Further details of the procurement process can be found within the tender documentation.
Participants who respond to the Tender Notice will be issued with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) as part of the Invitation to Participate (ITP) stage.

This is to enable providers to approach the Council and express their interest in being considered as the 'most suitable provider'.
The NHS Health Check programme aims to prevent cardiovascular disease (CVD) and associated conditions through the early assessment, awareness, and management of individual behavioural and physiological risk factors. The programme is aimed at all adults in England aged between 40-74 who are not currently being treated for CVD. 
The delivery of NHS Health Checks is a statutory responsibility for all Local Authorities (LAs). All eligible individuals must be invited to attend an NHS Health Check once every five years.
The current contract(s) for the delivery of NHS Health Checks lies solely with GP practices across the three LAs. In this financial year, 26/27, all 60 GP Practices across Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire, and Milton Keynes (13 25, 22 respectively) are contracted to deliver NHS Health Checks. However, uptake has remained consistently low for the last five years across all three LAs. In addition, we see lower uptake in more deprived communities, people from minority ethnic backgrounds, and men all of whom tend to access primary care services less frequently.
Low uptake of the NHS Health Check presents a number of risks to each LA, including failing to meet the nationally mandated targets, the inability to identify risk factors for CVD early and therefore missing opportunities for secondary prevention, and a worsening of health inequalities. 
A Milton Keynes Primary Care Network (PCN) community outreach offer is required, to supplement GP practice delivery, increase access and enhance the opportunities available for eligible patients to attend for an NHS Health Check at a venue within their own communities and/or within their workplace. 
PCNs are well-positioned to deliver this service as they already work closely with, and on behalf of, GP Practices. They have established access to relevant systems and strong working relationships, enabling a seamless pathway for patients to receive an NHS Health Check within a community setting.  For efficiencies to the service the expectation is there will be one lead PCN related organisation for contract management purposes and the delivery to the community from the Primary Care Networks. 
This approach ensures that, where required, patients can be effectively referred and supported to continue their care through their registered GP Practice following their NHS Health Check. In addition, the service presents an opportunity to build relationships, understanding and trust within communities, encouraging greater engagement with Primary Care services-not only for NHS Health Checks but for a wider range of health interventions.
Those patients who are out of area and whose patient record is not accessible by the provider will receive a paper copy of results and clear instructions to follow up with their own GP Practice
The community outreach offers will support each LA to meet their statutory responsibilities to deliver NHS Health Checks to the eligible population, aged 40-74 on a 5-year rolling basis and reducing health inequalities. It will enable us to meet local and national targets both in the number of NHS Health Checks offered, and those that receive an NHS Health Check. 
Who is eligible for an NHS Health Checks in community and workplaces
• 40-74, without an existing diagnosed CVD condition
• Not had an NHS Health Check in the last 5 years
• Resident in Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire and Milton Keynes and/or are registered with a GP practice within Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire and Milton Keynes local authority areas

tender.description:
NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board (referred to as the Commissioner) is inviting suitably qualified and experienced providers to express interest in delivering an Adult non-complex Audiology Service in Birmingham and Solihull.

Patients must be registered with a Birmingham and Solihull GP practice for whom Birmingham and Solihull (BSOL) Integrated Care Board (ICB) is the responsible commissioner.
